title: Ifast Business Bank
intro: iFAST Global Bank is a UK-regulated digital bank offering multi-currency accounts and high interest rates. You can hold GBP, USD, and EUR in one place and earn rewards while banking.
body: iFAST Global Bank is a UK-licensed digital bank (authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority).
It offers multi-currency current accounts (you can hold GBP, EUR, USD and other major currencies) and a numberless debit card to use for spending.
It launched its digital personal banking platform for the UK market in or around April 2023.
Good interest rates: For example, one of their current account offers carries ~3.50% AER on GBP, ~1.50% on EUR, ~2.80% on USD (variable) for UK customers.
Multi-currency convenience: If you deal with different currencies (travel, overseas spending, remittances) they make it easier.
Safety: Deposits are covered under the UK deposit-protection scheme (FSCS) up to £85000 just like many UK banks.
Modern digital features: App-based, including a card without visible numbers (for extra security) and support via digital channels.
**Why choose us (if you’re using our recommendation)?**
We’re recommending iFAST Global Bank because it ticks several boxes for people who:
Need banking that works across currencies or internationally
Prefer digital / app-first banks rather than traditional branch banking
Want to make their money do more (via interest) rather than just sitting idle
Want a UK-regulated bank (so you have protections) but with modern features
**Things to be aware of / possible drawbacks**
Because it is very digital and “newer” compared to big high-street banks, some services (branches, cash deposits, extensive legacy features) may be limited.
Offers like the high interest or cashback may be promotional (check the terms). For example, some users on Reddit noted that certain cashback offers were limited in time.
As with any bank, read the terms & conditions carefully (e.g., fees, card usage abroad, currency conversion).
Multi-currency accounts are great, but if you only use one currency in one country and prefer full branch service with cash etc., a traditional bank might still be simpler.
